title: ICC prosecutor requests arrest warrants for Israeli and Hamas leaders
body:
On 20 May 2024, the prosecutor of the International Criminal Court, Karim Khan, announced that he had requested arrest warrants for five people in connection with the war in Gaza and the 7 October 2023 attack. For Israel he named Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Yoav Gallant. For Hamas he named Yahya Sinwar, the group's leader in Gaza, Mohammed Deif, its military commander, and Ismail Haniyeh, its political leader based in Qatar.

The prosecutor sought warrants for the Hamas leaders on charges of war crimes and crimes against humanity, including the killing of civilians and the taking of hostages during the October 7 attack, and the maltreatment of and sexual violence against hostages. For Netanyahu and Gallant the charges included using starvation as a weapon of war and intentionally directing attacks against civilians. The requests had to be approved by a panel of ICC pre-trial judges before any warrant could be issued.

Netanyahu called it outrageous to compare Hamas with the Israeli army, which he described as the world's most moral. Benny Gantz, a member of the war cabinet, accused the prosecutor of moral blindness. President Joe Biden said there was no equivalence between Israel and Hamas, and Secretary of State Antony Blinken said Israel had not been given enough time to show that its own prosecutors were investigating. Hamas said it strongly denounced the requests, arguing that they equated victims with perpetrators.
